Dear Mr. Piper:

SUBJECT: Punahou School - Maintenance Shop

The Department of Health (DOH) has reviewed the following reports: 

1. TIER III Direct- Exposure Risk Assessment Report, dated October 28, 1996, and prepared by your office.

2. Residual Gasoline Constituents in Soil Resulting From a UST Release at Punahou School, 1601 Punahou Street, Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, 96822, dated January 5, 1995, and prepared by Brewer Environmental Services.

3. Soil Excavation, Punahou School, 1601 Punahou Street, Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, 96822, dated July 26, 1993, and prepared by Brewer Environmental Services.

Please note the reports have been placed with the public record for the facility.

This letter follows the March 24, 2006, telephone call and message left for you by  Mr. Shaobin Li of DOH, and conversations between Mr. Randy Overton, your Assistant Director, and Mr. Li on June 28, 2006, regarding the reporting status of the site.

According to the July 26, 1993, Soil Excavation report, as indicated in Table 2: 
Laboratory Analytical Results, BESD Job #3505 Punahou School, contaminated soil was present at soil sample 3505.W-wall at 14 feet depth below ground surface (bgs) in the subsurface soils.  Benzene was detected at a concentration of 46 mg/kg, and ethylbenzene at 137 mg/kg, higher than their respective DOH Tier 1 action levels.

Based on the information provided in the October 28, 1996, report, the extent of contaminated soil left in place was 25 cubic meters with thickness of two meters.  In response to your October 28, 1996, report, the DOH letter (U1052RB) stated the contaminated soil present under the paved area at the site can be safely managed in place without posing a potential threat to groundwater as long as the integrity of the pavement capping the soil is maintained. However, if pavement capping the soil is removed or the contaminated soil is otherwise exposed during development activities at the site then the soil should be re-sampled and managed in accordance with DOH guidelines (e.g., immediately recapped and/or excavated or remediated).   

The results of the investigation and any actions taken including groundwater monitoring and soil sampling results should be submitted to our office for review.  Please re-sample the areas of known soil contamination as indicated above to determine contaminant concentrations in soil, and submit your report(s) as soon as possible to this office.

We appreciate your cooperation and prompt attention to this matter.  If you have any questions regarding this letter, please contact Mr. Shaobin Li of our Underground Storage Tank Section at (808) 586-4226.

Sincerely,

STEVEN Y.K. CHANG, P.E., CHIEF
Solid and Hazardous Waste Branch

Based on the information submitted, we conclude that no further action is necessary for this release.  However, please note that state law requires any detectable level of petroleum contamination discovered in the sub-surface of current or former UST facilities to be reported to this office within 24 hours, including de minimis contamination, contamination found at concentrations lower than DOH Tier 1 action levels, and contamination found after receiving a "No Further Action" letter from DOH.  In addition, groundwater monitoring well(s) should be removed or closed according to the Department of Land and Natural Resources' well abandonment policy. Old or damaged monitoring wells are potential conduits for contamination to the groundwater aquifer, and liability lies with the owner/installer of the monitoring well(s) as well as the landowner. A report that documents the proper abandonment of the well(s) should be submitted to this office for inclusion in the public record for the facility.
 
If you have any questions regarding this letter, please contact Mr. Shaobin Li of our Underground Storage Tank Section at (808) 586-4226.
